description: When creating story maps from code, start with the outermost layer (entry points), analyze operations and domain concepts, create epics from higher-order goals, and lay out the story journey.
context: when extracting story maps from code

steps.title: Find Entry Points
checklist: CLI commands (main(), argparse)
UI entry points (routes, handlers, button clicks)
MCP server tools (names, parameters)
API contracts (REST, GraphQL, WSDL)
Acceptance tests (end-to-end, BDD)

steps.title: Analyze Operations and Domain
checklist: List operations from entry points
Identify MAJOR domain concepts (high-level entities)
Identify MINOR domain concepts (supporting entities)
Document relationships between concepts

steps.title: Create Epics from Goals
checklist: Group operations by higher-order goals (what is user trying to accomplish?)
Create epics from goals, NOT from class structure
Each epic represents a major capability
Example: Operations 'render-outline, render-increments' → Goal 'Render StoryGraph' → Epic 'Render StoryGraph'

steps.title: Create Sub-Epics from Behaviors
checklist: Identify distinct behaviors for each epic (different ways to accomplish goal)
Group behaviors into sub-epics
Example: Epic 'Render StoryGraph' → Sub-Epics 'Render Outline', 'Render Increments'

steps.title: Lay Out Story Journey
checklist: Trace code flow: Start (entry point) → Middle (operations) → End (completion)
For each story include: WHEN (trigger), WHY (purpose), OUTCOME (result), ACTOR (who)
Include error handling and alternative paths
Example: 'User invokes command' → 'System validates input' → 'System processes' → 'System confirms'

common_mistakes: Starting with internal classes instead of entry points
Creating epics from class structure instead of goals
Creating stories from every method call
